parts.text: Which claim correctly describes lines $p$ and $q$?

options.text: The answer is the phrase same plane.
Lines $p$ and $q$ are parallel because they lie on the same flat page.
Lines $p$ and $q$ are not parallel, because they meet when extended.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Nandini draws straight lines $p$ and $q$ on the same flat page. When she extends them, they cross at one point, and the gap between them shrinks as she nears that point.

part_answers.answer: Parallel lines on the same plane never meet when extended. Here $p$ and $q$ cross at one point, so they are not parallel.

teacher.key_rationale: Parallel lines lie on the same plane and never meet when extended. Nandini's lines meet, so they are not parallel. Naming 'same plane' alone or treating same-page as enough both miss the non-meeting test.
